title: Test whether one generator matches word-distribution information before and after shuffling pages
statement: On the public practice pages in binding order, the Montemurro–Zanette Eq. 2 statistic (https://doi.org/10.1371/journal.pone.0066344) gives 0.275 bits per word at 807 tokens in ZL (6,048 certain tokens) and 0.278 in Takahashi (5,973). I used block sizes 100, 200, 400, 807, 1600 and 2400, dropped the final incomplete block at each size and used the hypergeometric expectation under uniform global token shuffles of the retained stream. In ZL the six values are 0.208, 0.255, 0.270, 0.275, 0.187 and 0.156. In Takahashi they are 0.224, 0.268, 0.285, 0.278, 0.187 and 0.162. Against each transliteration I fit the unchanged repository grille, self-citation and Latin table-cipher generators on the public training partition, sampled seeds 1–8, and generated the same counts per line and page. Across the six sizes, every grille and Latin table-cipher seed undershoots the corresponding manuscript value and every self-citation seed overshoots it. At 807 in ZL the seed ranges are -0.008–0.010, -0.008–0.021 and 0.528–0.579 bits per word respectively. The public sample and ordering differ from the full, thematically reordered sample in the paper. At 807, eight shuffles of whole pages give 0.093–0.190 in ZL and 0.108–0.189 in Takahashi. Eight within-page token shuffles at fixed page order give 0.247–0.267 and 0.261–0.273. These controls motivate checking how much of the curve a generator produces through within-page reuse and how much comes from shared vocabulary between nearby pages.
check: Before evaluating a candidate, freeze its generator, seeds and block sizes. Use binding order and all certain tokens. At each size retain the largest prefix divisible into complete blocks, then compute sum(c log2 c) across nonzero block-by-token counts c divided by retained length. Subtract its expectation, computed by averaging c log2 c over the hypergeometric count in one block given each token's global total, then summing over token types and dividing by block size. Compare ZL and Takahashi at matched lengths across the six scales. Report paired differences from both page-order and within-page token shuffles using seeds 1–8, including the changes induced by dropping any incomplete final block. Choose the candidate and acceptance bands from the public training partition before independent confirmation.
